title: Investments: risk, return and asset pricing
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Measure returns and risk, build efficient portfolios with mean-variance analysis, use the CAPM, the security market line and multifactor models, test market efficiency, and understand how stocks, bonds and funds are analyzed and how performance is evaluated.

weeks.4: Mean-variance optimization and the efficient frontier

blocks.deliverable: Compute arithmetic, geometric and money-weighted returns.
Plot an efficient frontier in Python.
Estimate betas and alphas for five stocks.
Week 7 midterm; test a simple trading rule against the market.
Value a stock two ways and a bond one way.
Rank three funds by Sharpe, Treynor and alpha.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Portfolio case: for a given set of ten assets, estimate expected returns and covariances from historical data, build the efficient frontier and the tangency portfolio in Python, compare it with an equal-weighted portfolio out of sample, and write a three-page report on the results and their limits.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
